P_EAGER.summary: ExplorerService.setToCopy eagerly downloads every selected remote resource to a local temp directory before the clipboard write returns, blocking the Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X gesture with no size/count cap, no progress UI, no cancellation, and a sequential loop.

P_PATHLEAK.summary: The internal cacheHome temp path is written onto the system clipboard, leaking internal path layout to native paste targets.

P_CASESENS.summary: RemoteFileSystemProxyClient.capabilities hard-codes FileSystemProviderCapabilities.PathCaseSensitive instead of deriving it from the remote OS the way the sibling RemoteFileSystemProviderClient does.

P_CATCHDUP.summary: resolveClipboardResources' catch block pushes ALL remoteResources after the loop may already have pushed some temp targets, so a partial download failure produces duplicate and mixed-scheme clipboard entries.

P_ORDER.summary: resolveClipboardResources pushes all local resources first and remote temp targets after, so clipboard order no longer matches the user's selection order for mixed selections.

P_SILENTFALLBACK.summary: On remote-download failure the code falls back to remote URIs with only a logService.warn — no notification, progress, or telemetry — so native paste silently degrades with no user-visible signal.

cut_becomes_copy.summary: Cut (move) of a remote file degrades to a copy: setToCopy substitutes local temp file:// URIs, so the paste move-branch moves the temp copy and the original remote file is never removed.

temp_uri_breaks_workspace_identity.summary: Replacing the copied remote URI with a local temp file:// URI breaks the source's workspace identity, so same-folder duplicate/rename-on-paste in a remote workspace fails with 'already exists' instead of auto-incrementing.

remote_to_remote_roundtrip.summary: Discarding the original remote URIs makes remote-to-remote copy/paste regress to a download plus re-upload round-trip instead of a server-side remote copy.

tempdir_leak_local_only_copy.summary: cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir is called only inside the `remoteResources.length > 0` branch, so a remote copy followed by a local-only copy leaves the previous temp directory on disk.

dispose_unawaited_cleanup.summary: The synchronous dispose() calls the async cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir() without awaiting it — a floating promise whose deletion may never complete before teardown.

temp_deleted_clipboard_dangling.summary: The temp directory backing the OS clipboard is recursively deleted on dispose() or on the next remote copy, while the clipboard still points at those paths, so a later native paste yields missing/empty files.

tempdir_race_concurrent.summary: Overlapping setToCopy calls race the single unsynchronized remoteClipboardTempDir field, so a second copy's cleanup deletes the directory a still-running first copy is writing into.

empty_catch_cleanup.summary: cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir uses a literal empty `catch { }` that does not bind or log the error, so a failed del() silently leaves temp copies behind (and the field is reset regardless, discarding the only reference).

no_crash_cleanup_startup_sweep.summary: There is no crash cleanup and no startup sweep of stale cacheHome/remote-clipboard/* directories, so temp trees accumulate on disk indefinitely.

temp_plaintext_disk_security.summary: Remote file contents are materialized in plaintext under the persistent cacheHome/userDataPath with umask-default permissions and only best-effort cleanup, so potentially sensitive data persists on local disk.

jsdoc_file_uri_contract_violated.summary: resolveClipboardResources' JSDoc promises it returns file:// URIs for all resources, but the catch path returns the original remote-scheme URIs, so the documented contract is false exactly in the failure case.

temp_dir_wording_doc.summary: The 'temp'/'temp directory' wording in the comments could send a maintainer to os.tmpdir() when the copies actually live under environmentService.cacheHome.

no_telemetry_proxy_download.summary: There is no telemetry or metrics on the remote-download/proxy path, so a field report of 'remote paste doesn't work' cannot be triaged between download failure, routing failure, or temp cleanup.

tempdir_bare_slot_type.summary: remoteClipboardTempDir is a bare `URI | undefined` slot whose single-slot create-before-destroy lifecycle is maintained purely by convention rather than expressed in a type.

zero_tests_explorer_temp_download.summary: ExplorerService.resolveClipboardResources and the temp-dir lifecycle are untested — no coverage of the all-local passthrough, the download-failure fallback, or cleanup/dispose behavior.

basename_collision_untested.summary: The happy-path uuid-subfolder collision avoidance (two remote files sharing a basename getting distinct targets) exists but has no test pinning it.

scope_creep.summary: The PR goes beyond the linked bug: DND drag-text filtering, native-format read paths, and writing native formats for purely-local copies are additional scope.

double_paste_regression.summary: writeResources now writes OS-native file clipboard formats on ordinary internal local copies, so an in-app Ctrl+V also satisfies the explorer DOM paste listener's clipboardData.files guard, firing the paste a second time (double paste + spurious confirm dialog).

stale_format_shadowing.summary: writeClipboardBuffer writes one format without clearing the others, so a mixed/remote copy after an all-local copy can leave a stale native format on the clipboard and a native paste yields the previously-copied files.

has_vs_read_divergence.summary: hasResources() reports true on mere presence of a native clipboard format while readResources() filters/parses to file:// URIs and can return [], so the Explorer Paste affordance is enabled for a paste that silently does nothing.

win_multifile_filenamew.summary: Windows native file-clipboard interop is single-file only: FileNameW is written only when resources.length === 1 (and read back as one path), so multi-file copies fall through to the VS Code custom format and native Explorer paste produces nothing, with no user signal.

macos_binary_plist.summary: plistToFiles parses NSFilenamesPboardType with an XML-plist regex, but macOS/Finder typically serializes that pasteboard type as a binary plist, so pasting Finder-copied files silently returns nothing.

plist_handrolled_parser.summary: The hand-rolled string-concatenation plist writer and regex reader duplicate the existing plistParser.ts and handle only 3 of 5 XML entities with no schema — a fragile stringly-typed serialization.

plist_empty_string_regex.summary: plistToFiles' `<string>([^<]+)</string>` regex requires at least one character, so a well-formed empty `<string></string>` element is silently dropped and the output length no longer matches the input.

urilist_all_or_nothing_parse.summary: uriListToFiles runs `.map(URI.parse)` over every line inside a single try/catch, so one malformed line discards every valid file:// entry and returns an empty list.

urilist_filter_untested.summary: uriListToFiles does filter to file:// URIs, but that filtering (mixed vscode-remote/http entries, # comments, blank lines) has no test, so a regression dropping the filter would go unnoticed.

parsers_no_logging.summary: plistToFiles/uriListToFiles/fileNameWToFile (and readResources) all catch and return [] with no logging at all, so a parser bug is indistinguishable from an empty clipboard and a regression stays permanently invisible.

filenamew_odd_byteoffset.summary: fileNameWToFile constructs a Uint16Array over the delivered VSBuffer's backing store at a byteOffset that is frequently odd, which throws RangeError; the surrounding catch swallows it so Windows native paste silently returns nothing.

fromcharcode_spread_rangeerror.summary: String.fromCharCode(...u16.subarray(...)) spreads an externally-sized array, so a very long path or a payload without a null terminator can exceed the engine's argument limit and throw a RangeError that is swallowed into an empty paste.

utf16_endianness_comment.summary: The comment 'Uint16Array naturally uses the platform's char encoding (UTF-16)' is technically wrong and hides the load-bearing assumption: correctness depends on the host being little-endian, not on any encoding property of Uint16Array.

charcodeat_surrogate_pairs.summary: filePathToUtf16LE uses charCodeAt so non-BMP characters pass through as raw code units — it works only by luck for UTF-16LE and the assumption is not expressed as an invariant.

default_branch_comment_wrong.summary: The '// Default (Windows, or mixed local/remote)' comment is inaccurate on both halves: Windows single-file never reaches it, and macOS/Linux also fall through for any non-all-local set.

electron_oneformat_comment.summary: The rationale comment 'Electron's clipboard API only supports one buffer format per call' over-generalizes and misattributes the limit — clipboard.write() can set several formats, and the restriction belongs to the writeClipboardBuffer wrapper.

clipboard_format_literals_ifladder.summary: The four clipboard formats are loose string literals and the platform-to-format selection is an if-ladder repeated in write/read/has, so the platform x format matrix is not a single checkable structure.

linux_uri_list_literal.summary: LINUX_FILE_FORMAT hard-codes the raw 'text/uri-list' string, duplicating the Mimes.uriList constant that is referenced symbolically elsewhere, including in dnd.ts which this PR also touches.

gnome_copied_files_format.summary: GNOME/Nautilus paste expects the x-special/gnome-copied-files format with a copy/cut verb line rather than plain text/uri-list, so the Linux write path may not be honored by the main Linux file managers.

native_format_interop_unverified.summary: Whether NSFilenamesPboardType, text/uri-list, and FileNameW written via Electron's writeBuffer are actually honored by Finder / GNOME-KDE file managers / Explorer is unverifiable from the diff and needs a manual per-OS test pass.

clipboard_codec_design_testability.summary: The five clipboard codec helpers are private and only reachable through platform-branching public methods, and their 'always file:// URIs' contract is implicit; extracting exported free functions / a shared toFileURIs helper would make both checkable.

zero_tests_clipboard_codecs.summary: The clipboard encode/decode helpers and the platform dispatch in writeResources/readResources/hasResources ship with zero unit tests despite being pure, byte-level, and format-sensitive.

magic_number_bytelength_guard.summary: The `buffer.byteLength < 4` guard uses an unexplained magic number (one UTF-16 char plus a two-byte null terminator).

missing_trace_logging_clipboard.summary: The rewritten writeResources/readResources/hasResources omit the class-wide logService.trace('NativeClipboardService#method') opener present on every other public method.

explorer_writeresources_blast_radius.summary: The native OS clipboard write now applies to every writeResources([localFile]) caller, so unrelated callers such as chat widgets now populate the native file clipboard — a broadened, untracked blast radius.

clipboard_paste_arbitrary_path_read.summary: Pasting clipboard-supplied file:// paths allows user-gesture-driven reads of arbitrary local paths.

dnd_remote_text_regression.summary: Narrowing DataTransfers.TEXT to file:// resources means dragging a remote (SSH/WSL/container) resource into an in-app text target such as the terminal, search, or an editor now sets no text at all.

dnd_webloc_comment_imprecise.summary: The .webloc rationale comment is imprecise: it says 'remote URIs' when the value placed in TEXT is a getUriLabel label, states macOS .webloc creation as definite OS behavior, and justifies only the macOS case though the filter applies on all platforms.

dnd_filter_untested.summary: The new Schemas.file filter on the DND TEXT transfer (all-remote leaves TEXT unset, mixed selections) is a user-visible behavior change with no test.

dnd_schemas_import_unverified.summary: Schemas is used in dnd.ts with no visible import in the shown diff hunk — flagged as a cannot-verify-from-diff note.

provider_reregistration_leak.summary: RemoteFileSystemProxyClient.register constructs and registers a new provider inside the onWillActivateFileSystemProvider listener with no idempotency guard, so every vscode-remote operation after the first throws 'already registered' (swallowed and logged at error level) and leaks a provider into the window-lifetime DisposableStore.

register_catch_swallows_failure.summary: The registration catch logs at error but the async IIFE resolves normally, so activation appears to succeed with no provider and the next access fails with a generic 'No file system provider found' far from the cause.

proxy_no_streaming_readfile.summary: The proxy advertises only FileReadWrite (no streaming), so readFile returns the entire file as one VSBuffer forwarded across two IPC hops with no size cap — the whole file materializes in memory in each process.

readonly_type_overclaims.summary: The client implements IFileSystemProviderWithFileReadWriteCapability and advertises FileReadWrite while carrying Readonly as a runtime capability bit and throwing on all mutators, so the type advertises the opposite of the intent; the intentional combination also lacks a doc comment.

plain_error_readonly_methods.summary: writeFile/mkdir/delete/rename throw a plain Error instead of createFileSystemProviderError / NotSupportedError with NoPermissions, so the error classifies as Unknown and bypasses downstream error-code handling; the message is also developer-oriented.

watch_inert_undocumented.summary: watch()/onDidChangeFile are permanently inert with no comment or capability flag saying so, while the provider is registered scheme-wide for vscode-remote — and it mixes conventions (mutators throw, watch silently returns Disposable.None).

client_duplicates_diskfsproviderclient.summary: The client hand-rolls stat/readdir/readFile channel forwarding that duplicates the canonical DiskFileSystemProviderClient base class the sibling RemoteFileSystemProviderClient extends.

client_trusts_wire_no_validation.summary: stat/readFile trust the wire with no revival or validation — IChannel.call<T> infers T from the caller's own annotation, so `const buffer: VSBuffer` and `Promise<IStat>` are unverified against what the server actually returns.

remoteauthority_guard_comment.summary: The loop-prevention guard comment says the window 'has its own remote connection' but the code only checks the static remoteAuthority config value, papering over the connected-versus-configured distinction.

client_docstring_overclaims.summary: The class docstring's claim that it 'enables copy/paste and drag-and-drop of files between remote and local workspaces' is unscoped — the Explorer copy path pre-downloads to file:// URIs and never exercises this class.

trace_logs_resource_paths.summary: The new logService.trace calls log full resource paths (user data) on every proxied operation.

zero_tests_proxy_client.summary: RemoteFileSystemProxyClient is entirely untested — the loop-prevention register() guard, the read-only throwing mutators, the readFile VSBuffer unwrap, and the capabilities contract all lack coverage.

routing_hang_no_timeout.summary: The forwarded call can hang forever: findWindowForAuthority does no liveness check and IPCServer.getChannel falls back to an unbounded wait for a future matching connection, so routing to a closing, crashed, or not-yet-started window never resolves or rejects (unlike the fail-fast NodeRemoteResourceRouter).

authority_case_compare.summary: findWindowForAuthority compares remoteAuthority with strict === instead of the codebase's case-insensitive isEqualAuthority, so a case-differing authority fails to match the owning window.

proxy_no_caller_auth.summary: The main handler ignores the caller's connection context and routes purely on the payload URI's authority with no authorization, scoping, or Workspace-Trust check, so any renderer can read arbitrary files from another window's privileged remote connection (confused deputy).

window_ctx_magic_string.summary: The `window:${id}` connection-context format is an untyped cross-process contract reconstructed inline here and duplicated across many sites, documented only in a comment with no shared constant, so a producer-side change breaks routing silently.

unvalidated_args_uri_revive.summary: `const args = arg as unknown[]` then `URI.revive(args[0] as UriComponents)` indexes an unvalidated optional parameter, so a missing or malformed arg surfaces as a raw TypeError instead of a clean domain error (the proxy server repeats the same cast).

duplicate_authority_first_match.summary: Authority-to-window routing is a first-match linear scan, so when two windows share a remote authority the selection is arbitrary; the code never establishes that authority-to-window is 1:1.

adhoc_narrow_interfaces.summary: The testability interfaces (IRemoteFileSystemProxyWindowsService / IRemoteFileSystemProxyIPCServer) use anonymous inline shapes that are not Pick<>-derived from the real services and are re-declared verbatim in the tests, and findWindowForAuthority returns a freshly-built `{ id: number }` literal rather than the matched window.

startup_race_channel_not_ready.summary: The target window's proxy server channel may not be registered yet when the main handler routes to it during startup, so the call rejects with an unknown-channel error until renderer init finishes, with no retry or readiness wait.

no_command_allowlist.summary: The main handler is a pure untyped passthrough with no command allow-list, so it forwards any command string to another renderer's file-serving channel; the only structural check is the URI scheme.

cancellation_token_dropped.summary: RemoteFileSystemProxyMainHandler.call forwards command and arg but drops IServerChannel's 4th cancellationToken parameter when calling the target renderer channel.

handrolled_routing_not_iclientrouter.summary: Routing is hand-rolled inside IServerChannel.call instead of implementing the codebase's canonical IClientRouter (as NodeRemoteResourceRouter and URLHandlerRouter do), which also adds an extra channel hop.

main_handler_edge_cases_untested.summary: Main-handler edge cases are untested: empty windows list, duplicate remoteAuthority, a plain UriComponents payload exercising URI.revive, and the listen() guard throw.

no_typed_rpc_contract.summary: The proxy RPC boundary has no shared typed contract: the shared module exports only channel-name strings, each of the three hops re-types the command literals and takes `arg?: any` with positional unchecked casts, so command/arity drift is invisible to the compiler.

channel_name_spelling_convention.summary: The new channel-name string values spell 'FileSystem' as two camelCased words while the closest sibling channel-name constants collapse it to 'Filesystem'.

routing_test_underasserts.summary: The 'routes call to correct window' test asserts only the selected window ctx — it never varies the target id nor asserts the forwarded command/arg, the channel name, or the propagated return value, so a forwarding regression would still pass.

test_fixture_weak_discrimination.summary: The window fixtures lack discriminating power — only one window carries a matching remoteAuthority and there is no near-miss/decoy authority — so an implementation ignoring the authority, or a regression from strict equality to startsWith/includes, would still pass.

test_error_regex_coupling.summary: The assert.rejects regexes match only the fixed error-message prefix (never the interpolated authority/scheme), coupling the tests to prose that is not a stable contract while missing wrong-value bugs.

test_file_name_mismatch.summary: The file is named remoteFileSystemProxy.test.ts but only tests the main handler, so its name implies coverage of the whole proxy subsystem; the codebase convention names test files after the source file under test.

uri_revive_wire_path_untested.summary: Every test passes a real URI instance, so URI.revive only exercises its instanceof fast path and the from-wire UriComponents reconstruction branch that real IPC uses is never tested.

dead_exists_resolve.summary: The proxy server dispatches 'exists' and 'resolve' commands (plus resolve's IFileStatWithMetadata plumbing) that no client ever invokes — unreachable, untested, speculative surface on a cross-renderer channel.

server_layering_inconsistent.summary: The server mixes abstraction levels: stat/readdir call the low-level fileService.getProvider(scheme) directly while readFile/exists/resolve go through IFileService, so provider activation, limits, events, and error normalization apply on some paths but not others.

server_plain_error_no_code.summary: The server's stat/readdir/readFile throw a plain Error instead of createFileSystemProviderError with a FileSystemProviderErrorCode, so the typed error code is lost as it propagates back through FileService.

server_type_annotations_inaccurate.summary: The server's stat() hand-declares the structural literal { type; size; mtime; ctime } instead of the canonical IStat (dropping permissions the client's typed stat claims), and resolve() carries a forced `as Promise<IFileStatWithMetadata>` cast that the runtime resolveMetadata flag does not guarantee.

server_jsdoc_link_rot.summary: The server class JSDoc has two {@link} targets that are not imported (so they won't resolve and a rename won't flag them), explains the design solely by pointing at ElectronRemoteResourceLoader, and overstates 'Registered in every renderer process'.

server_no_scheme_validation.summary: The renderer-side proxy server performs no scheme validation of its own — the vscode-remote-only guardrail lives solely in the main-process handler — a defense-in-depth gap that would become an arbitrary local-file-read confused deputy if any future caller forwarded a file:// URI.

no_audit_trail_server.summary: Cross-window remote file reads produce no audit trail on the serving side, so exfiltration through the proxy would be unattributable and an incident could not be reconstructed.

zero_tests_proxy_server.summary: RemoteFileSystemProxyServer is entirely untested — the command-dispatch switch, the unknown-command throw, the listen() throw, and the missing-provider throws all lack coverage.

zero_tests_broad_sweep.summary: The PR's most novel logic ships with essentially no tests — the proxy client, the proxy server dispatch, the clipboard format round-trips, and the explorerService temp-download path — with only main-handler routing covered.

app_desktop_wiring_untested.summary: The DI wiring in app.ts and desktop.main.ts (channel registration, server + client instantiation) has no test coverage.

no_feature_flag_kill_switch.summary: The main handler, per-window server/client, and native-clipboard writes are wired unconditionally with no feature flag or kill switch, leaving no runtime off-switch short of a full revert.
